name: Ahaziah
bio:
Ahaziah, son of Ahab and successor to his throne, began to reign over Israel in Samaria in Jehoshaphat's seventeenth year as king of Judah, reigning two years (1 Kings 22:51). He did evil in the LORD's eyes, walking in the ways of his father Ahab, his mother Jezebel, and Jeroboam son of Nebat, serving and worshipping Baal just as his father had done (1 Kings 22:52-53). He later asked Jehoshaphat to let his servants sail with Jehoshaphat's trading fleet to Ophir, but Jehoshaphat refused (1 Kings 22:49).

## 📖 Core Story: A Fatal Fall and a Dying King's Defiance

After Ahab's death, Moab rebelled against Israel. Ahaziah then fell through a lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria and was injured; instead of seeking the LORD, he sent messengers to ask Baalzebub, the god of Ekron, whether he would recover. The LORD sent Elijah to intercept the messengers with a counter-message: because Ahaziah had sought a foreign god instead of the God of Israel, he would not leave his bed alive (2 Kings 1:1-4).

When the messengers returned early and explained a man had turned them back with this message, Ahaziah sent a captain with fifty men to bring Elijah down from the hill where he sat; fire fell from heaven and consumed them. A second captain and his fifty met the same end. A third captain pleaded for mercy, and at the angel of the LORD's word Elijah went down with him unharmed to deliver the same verdict to Ahaziah's face: because he had sent to Baalzebub instead of Israel's God, he would surely die. He did, exactly as the LORD had spoken through Elijah, and since he had no son, his brother Jehoram succeeded him as king of Israel (2 Kings 1:5-18).
